attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT strips every trailing ')' unconditionally, so URLs whose paths legitimately end in a balanced parenthesis (e.g. Wikipedia-style links) are linked to a truncated address that will likely 404.

The fallback hard-cuts a text token mid-word when no whitespace fits and nothing has been emitted yet. That contradicts the PR's stated guarantee that truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens, and the test named 'never splits a link or a word' asserts the mid-word split.
attacks.evidence: else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') }); ... expect(truncate(tokenize('x'.repeat(400)), 280).tokens).toEqual([{ kind: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(280) }]);

attacks.claim: When the whitespace match is at index 0 (cut === 0), the code falls through to the mid-word hard cut instead of emitting nothing, so a leading space followed by a long word is split.

The budget is measured in UTF-16 code units (value.length) on the normal path but in code points (Array.from) on the hard-cut path, so the limit is inconsistent and surrogate-pair text can exceed the intended UTF-16 limit.

ItemDescription has no key tied to the item and is rendered without one in ItemPage, so expanded state can persist when navigating between items with long descriptions if the component instance is reused.

The toggle changes its visible label between 'Show more' and 'Show less' while also setting aria-expanded, so assistive tech announces both a changing name and the state. A fixed label with aria-expanded is the usual pattern.
Links open in a new tab with target="_blank", and nothing tells assistive-technology users this, so the new-tab behavior is unannounced for links whose text is the raw URL.

attacks.claim: Long unbroken URLs are rendered whole as link text with no wrapping rules in the diff, so on narrow screens a single long URL may overflow the text column. This predates the PR, since plain-text URLs already rendered unbroken in the same class, and the stylesheet is not part of the artifact, so the risk cannot be confirmed from the diff.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no overflow-wrap or word-break added to .item-description__body or the new anchor; the stylesheet is not in the diff.

attacks.claim: A description that begins with a long link is never collapsed, because the leading link is kept whole. A long product URL at the top therefore keeps the 'Request to borrow' button far down the screen, which is the problem the PR targets. This is an explicit design choice in the code.
